utility.notes: Entergy Mississippi is the well-established dominant electric utility for Jackson, the state capital.

value.name: Entergy Mississippi, LLC
value.notes: Entergy Mississippi is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

county.notes: Jackson, the Mississippi state capital, is primarily located in Hinds County (with small portions extending into Madison and Rankin counties).

permit_authority.value: City of Jackson Building Permits Division

interconnection_url.notes: Entergy Mississippi's own page confirms monthly net-metering credits carry over to the next billing cycle, with customers receiving a cash refund of any remaining credit balance only upon disconnecting from the Solar Net Metering program (not on an ongoing basis). The exact per-kWh credit valuation was not stated on this page and was not independently confirmed this session, so it is left unstated rather than assumed to be full retail rate.

battery_programs.notes: No confirmed financial battery storage incentive program was found on Entergy Mississippi's own net metering page or the City's own building permit page this session.

Separate electrical trade permit, pulled by a licensed professional
Entergy Interconnection Application and Agreement (Level 1, for systems <=20kW)
value.required_when: always, submitted via the Entergy Interconnection Portal or by mail

required_documents.notes: No Jackson-specific solar PV permit checklist or document list was found this session (unlike some other cities researched this marathon that publish a dedicated solar handout) — the City's general building/electrical-permit requirements are recorded here alongside Entergy Mississippi's own, more detailed, net-metering application requirements.

inspection_steps.notes: The City's own Building Permits Division page states the division generally handles 'permit applications, plan reviews, issuance, and inspections,' but no solar- or electrical-specific inspection sequence was published on the page fetched this session.

timeline_days.notes: Entergy Mississippi's own net metering page does not state a specific application-to-approval business-day timeline ('Processing timelines not specified on this page'), and no City of Jackson permit review timeline was published on the page fetched this session.

value.program_or_pathway: Level 1 Interconnection under the Entergy Mississippi Solar Net Metering Program — systems 20kW or less for residential customers.
other_conditions: System capacity cannot exceed 110% of the customer's prior calendar-year annual energy (kWh) usage.
Panels must be roof-mounted or facility-based behind the meter — ground-mounted or remote systems are not eligible under this program.
Customers with collective billing accounts are not eligible.
